scope: An initial Gospel-person index, not a complete biblical biographical dictionary. People are identified by explicit narrative references; selected event links are pointers to relevant study entries, not proofs of historicity. Alias matches are not identity equivalences. Scriptural claims and independent historical corroboration remain distinct.
sourcePolicy: Person summaries and relationships use cited canonical Gospel passages as primary narrative sources. External biography and historical claims have not been independently peer reviewed. Do not infer relationships beyond the stated references.

people.name: Jesus of Nazareth
people.disambiguation: The Jesus described by the four canonical Gospels, not any other person named Jesus.
people.summary: The Gospel narratives present Jesus teaching, healing and travelling through Galilee and Judea, culminating in the passion and resurrection accounts. The event links below are selected examples from the 79-entry map, not a complete list of his activities.

people.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
people.disambiguation: Mary the mother of Jesus, distinct from Mary Magdalene and Mary of Bethany.
people.summary: Luke and Matthew associate Mary with Jesus' birth and childhood. John places his mother at the wedding in Cana and at the crucifixion.

people.name: Joseph of Nazareth
people.disambiguation: Joseph, husband of Mary in the infancy accounts, not Joseph of Arimathea.
people.summary: Matthew describes Joseph receiving a warning and taking Mary and Jesus to Egypt, then returning to settle in Nazareth.

people.name: John the Baptist
people.disambiguation: The prophetic baptiser, distinct from John son of Zebedee.
people.summary: The Gospels portray John as a wilderness preacher who baptises Jesus and directs others' attention toward him.

people.name: Simon Peter
people.disambiguation: Simon called Peter, distinct from other men named Simon.
people.summary: Introduced as Andrew's brother, Peter appears in the fishermen narratives, Caesarea Philippi confession and resurrection accounts.

people.name: Andrew the apostle
people.disambiguation: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, among Jesus' first disciples.
people.summary: John identifies Andrew as a follower who brings Simon to Jesus; Mark recounts the fishermen's calling.

people.name: James son of Zebedee
people.disambiguation: One of multiple biblical men named James; the brother of John son of Zebedee.
people.summary: The Synoptic Gospels place James among the fishermen called by Jesus and among those present at the transfiguration.

people.name: John son of Zebedee
people.disambiguation: The disciple among the sons of Zebedee, distinct from John the Baptist.
people.summary: The Synoptic Gospels describe John as James' brother and a participant in the transfiguration. Authorship of the Fourth Gospel is not assumed by this profile.

people.name: Philip the disciple
people.disambiguation: Philip called by Jesus in John 1, not Philip the evangelist in Acts.
people.summary: In John's account Philip is called during the journey into Galilee and speaks with Nathanael.

people.name: Nathanael
people.disambiguation: Nathanael in the Fourth Gospel; identification with Bartholomew is not established by these passages.
people.summary: John records Philip inviting Nathanael to meet Jesus. This entry does not equate him automatically with Bartholomew.

people.name: Nicodemus
people.disambiguation: The Nicodemus named in the Gospel of John.
people.summary: John portrays Nicodemus speaking with Jesus, later appearing in council discussion and the burial account.

people.name: The Samaritan woman
people.disambiguation: The unnamed Samaritan woman in John 4; no personal name is supplied by the Gospel.
people.summary: John reports an exchange with Jesus at Jacob's well. Later traditional names are not presented here as biblical identification.

people.name: Jairus
people.disambiguation: The synagogue official named Jairus, not a different ruler or father.
people.summary: Mark and Luke describe Jairus requesting help for his daughter in an episode also involving a woman seeking healing.

people.name: The Capernaum centurion
people.disambiguation: The unnamed military officer in the servant-healing account.
people.summary: Matthew and Luke describe a centurion's appeal concerning a servant, with differences in how messengers are represented.

people.name: The Syrophoenician woman
people.disambiguation: The unnamed woman in Mark 7 and Matthew 15; Gospel descriptions use different ethnic terminology.
people.summary: Mark and Matthew recount her request for her daughter's deliverance in the region of Tyre.

people.name: Lazarus of Bethany
people.disambiguation: Brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, not the Lazarus in Luke 16's parable.
people.summary: John narrates the raising of Lazarus and places him with his sisters in Bethany.

people.name: Martha of Bethany
people.disambiguation: The Martha named as a sister of Lazarus and Mary, not a generic unnamed host.
people.summary: John presents Martha speaking with Jesus before the Lazarus episode and serving at a later meal in Bethany.

people.name: Mary of Bethany
people.disambiguation: Sister of Martha and Lazarus, not Mary Magdalene or Jesus' mother.
people.summary: John describes Mary alongside her family and records an anointing in Bethany. Whether this matches every other anointing narrative remains debated.

people.name: Mary Magdalene
people.disambiguation: Mary Magdalene, distinguished from Jesus' mother and Mary of Bethany.
people.summary: Luke names Mary Magdalene among women accompanying Jesus. John places her at the empty tomb and in the garden encounter.

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.disambiguation: The tax collector named in Luke 19.
people.summary: Luke recounts Zacchaeus meeting Jesus in Jericho and hosting him.

people.name: Bartimaeus
people.disambiguation: The named blind man in Mark's Jericho episode; parallel accounts differ in details.
people.summary: Mark names Bartimaeus as a blind beggar near Jericho. His name is not supplied in Luke's parallel.

people.name: Thomas the disciple
people.disambiguation: Thomas, called Didymus, among Jesus' disciples.
people.summary: John describes Thomas' absence at one gathering and his encounter with Jesus at a later appearance.

people.name: Judas Iscariot
people.disambiguation: Judas Iscariot, distinct from other men named Judas in the New Testament.
people.summary: The passion accounts portray Judas arranging to betray Jesus and identifying him at the arrest.

people.name: Pontius Pilate
people.disambiguation: The Roman prefect named in the trial and crucifixion narratives.
people.summary: The Gospels present Pilate as the Roman authority involved in Jesus' hearing and crucifixion sentence.

people.name: Caiaphas
people.disambiguation: The high priest identified in Matthew and John, distinct from Annas.
people.summary: The passion narratives name Caiaphas in the proceedings concerning Jesus.
